observations.claim: A normal quote takes about 45 minutes and the desk does about 30 a week, working from per-lane rate-card spreadsheets on the shared drive (self reported).
observations.quote: 45 minutes for a normal one. We do about 30 a week.

observations.claim: Quote effort varies from about 20 minutes (repeat lane) to over an hour (new lane or customs complications); the sales lead disputes both the sponsor's 20-minute figure and the process note's 30-minute target as describing only the easy cases.
observations.quote: A new lane means hunting for rates, and anything with customs complications means asking Femi, and now you're at an hour plus.

observations.claim: Accepted quotes reach operations as the forwarded email chain because the agreed details are scattered through the thread.
observations.quote: I forward the thread to operations. The whole chain, because the details are scattered through it

observations.claim: A large tender means two people copying between formats for most of a week, with about one in four won (self reported).
observations.quote: That's two people for most of a week, copying between their format and ours.

scale.load: a two-hundred-lane tender spreadsheet per major prospect

observations.claim: AI is deliberately kept away from rates for fear of invented numbers; a scoped read of the actual rate cards only is the stated condition for changing that.
observations.quote: if it invents a number we eat the difference. If it could read the actual rate cards and only the actual rate cards, that changes things.
observations.stated_dependencies: read the actual rate cards and only the actual rate cards
